scope: Local connected sample, offline allow-scripts iframe; actual Codex preview policy unknown.
checks: Receipt accepts chosen products and quantities across two destinations; only those shared stock rows increase.
Issue of 12 water and 3 cola immediately reduces the source, waits separately, then increases the selected receiver only after confirmation; Enter executes once.
Return uses the same inventory, starts with the warehouse role, and the source receiver confirms the returned multiitem quantity.
A local waste report leaves stock unchanged until the warehouse responsible person confirms review and finalizes it.

Shift count expected values equal the shared stock after all preceding work; empty values are rejected, submission only waits for review, warehouse approval applies the one-unit difference, and history retains all 10 steps.

When waste recorded after count submission already resolves its one-unit shortage, the warehouse role closes the count with adjustment none and stock is not deducted twice; a correction choice has no default.

An existing pending waste report permits starting and submitting a clearly provisional count; approval stays blocked until that report is resolved, then adjustment none closes without a second deduction.

Returning 8 wine bottles and 3.5 dl keeps two distinct confirmation labels with their original units, converts to 6 plus 0.35 litres, and changes the shared stocks by 6.35 litres. Warehouse/kitchen receivers do not see a mandatory bar shift-count task.

Empty/unreviewed receipts, duplicate documents, same-location moves, negative/fractional/excess quantity and over-receipt are blocked; wrong-location receivers have no task. Partial 4/3 receipt leaves one pending, and an explained source correction restores it once without waste.
The explicitly marked POS sample changes drink and recipe stock once; replaying the same sample changes neither inventory nor history, and the local receiver cannot launch it.
All accessible task, stock and history pages fit 1280, 1024, 768 and 390 pixels for both roles; hidden role-specific actions stay omitted.
Classic standalone artifact runs with no external requests or script errors while offline under inline-only CSP and an allow-scripts sandbox.
